articles.author: Hank Berrien
articles.summary: Dolly Parton, the towering queen of country music whose sky-high blonde wigs, razor-sharp wit, and world-class talent conquered pop culture and warmed millions of hearts, has passed away. She was 80. The tragic news was confirmed via an official Instagram video by her nephew, Bryan Seaver, on behalf of the Parton family. Parton’s death comes after a public struggle with her health. Fans were hit with a scare in September 2025 when she abruptly canceled a slated six-night Las Vegas residency at Caesars Palace. At the time, she cracked a classic Dolly joke to ease the blow, claiming it was just time for her “100,000-mile check-up” that didn’t involve her plastic surgeon. She asked for time to “get show ready,” reassuring the world that God hadn’t told her to quit the biz just yet. Shortly after, however, she bowed out of accepting her Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award in person at the Motion Picture Academy’s Governors Awards. Even while battling health issues, you couldn’t keep Parton down just this past summer; she was hard at work in Nashville overseeing “Dolly: An Original Musical,” an autobiographical stage production tracking her wild life that was meant to debut in 2026. articles.title: Mystery Swirls as U.S. Military Plane Lands in Moscow
articles.author: Ewan Palmer
articles.summary: Ricardo Arduengo/Reuters A U.S. military transport plane has unexpectedly landed in Moscow, sparking speculation about what the aircraft was carrying and why it was sent to Russia. Flight tracking service Flightradar24 shows that a Boeing C-17A Globemaster III, a U.S. military transport aircraft, arrived at Vnukovo International Airport on Tuesday morning. The flight originated at the U.S. Air Force facility in Camp Springs, Maryland, near Washington, D.C., where Andrews Air Force Base is located. It stopped at Charleston International Airport in South Carolina before flying to Riga, the capital of Latvia, on Sunday. The plane then continued its journey and landed in Russia’s capital around 10 a.m. Moscow time (2 a.m. ET) on Tuesday. Read more at The Daily Beast.

stories.summary: Confidence index drops to 89.4 in August from 90.2 in July amid frustration after five years of elevated inflation Americans’ confidence in the economy declined again this month as the ongoing conflict in Iran continued to push US gasoline prices above $4 per gallon. The Conference Board said on Tuesday that its consumer confidence index dipped to 89.4 in August from 90.2 in July. That was the lowest level in seven months but was essentially within the same lukewarm range it has been in since the beginning of the year. In late 2024 and early 2025, readings were consistently above 100. Continue reading...
